name: scroll-area
behavior: None — a native scroll container with custom-drawn scrollbars. The viewport must stay keyboard-scrollable: it receives tabindex=0 (and a visible focus ring) whenever its content holds no focusable children, so keyboard-only users can reach it (WCAG 2.1.1), and it is labelled when it scrolls. The custom scrollbars are decorative (aria-hidden) and only replace the native ones visually — native scrolling, wheel, touch and scroll-anchoring behaviour are never intercepted, and the thumb is draggable with the pointer only.

anatomyNotes: shadcn ScrollArea (Radix Root/Viewport/Scrollbar/Thumb/Corner) is the source; Salt has no scroll-area component — its panels and lists use native overflow — so the intersection is taken against native scrolling, and that is exactly what makes the optional parts optional: a theme may declare 'native scrollbars' as a constraint and render only root+viewport, losing no behavior. Overlay versus always-visible scrollbars is a RECIPE on scrollbar (opacity/timing), not anatomy. Scroll shadows or fade masks, where a theme uses them, are recipe on root.
